record_notes.DCP-LETT-13833: Incomplete fragment assigned November 1847–1851 from Hooker expedition; XML broad November 1, 1847 to December 31, 1851 is not a uniquely dated November letter. Three surviving blocks, five footnotes and bibliography read. Attribution to Owen supported by original notation but not corroborated by scolding episode. Body begins before of Whewell; I had not heard prefix supplied in a different hand, presumably Owen, and editorial synopsis must not turn it into unqualified Darwin prose. Whewell criticism explanation conjectural. Hooker novelties anticipated, not collected material already seen. Date, period and mixed source-layer hold.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13834: December 23 in mutually exclusive 1847–1854 years, eight discrete dates. Four blocks and five footnotes. Missing Carcharias tooth previously searched for; Darwin almost certain showed Owen, only rather thinks left it with him. Custody at College unproved, small attached number possibly removed. Possible connection to 13872 Coquimbo shells editorial suggestion, not recipient identity proof or direct reply. Corrects FitzRoy exaggeration of glacier wave retrospectively; body colonial language remains historical author voice. Exact-year and period held.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1484: July 17, supplied 1852. Six blocks, eight footnotes and bibliography. Forwarding correspondence to Captain Nelson by this post is intention; expected abstract expressly presumption, not actual appearance. Owen praise available, medium and complete wording absent. Darwin defends repeatedly observed males and homology while regretting inadequate illustration and finding systematics tedious; later 1854 fuller anatomy not already written here. Dana assent reported, missing communication not replaced with earlier disagreement letter. June London call missed Owen, not completed oral meeting.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1526F: July 30, supplied 1853; XML ALS two pages but preserved HTML explicitly says transcript not yet available. Sole extracted block is editorial synopsis of Sulivan address, copy-delivery request and Eastbourne weather, not Darwin quotation. Full available source record inspected; no surviving body to attest or export. No manuscript viewed and no promised book receipt inferred.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1662: April 7, supplied 1855. Seven blocks, eleven footnotes and bibliography. Darwin saw peas at Kew under misleading labels; his then belief in Berkeley pollen-affected specimens preserved without importing later correction. Forty-one reputed varieties planned in two or three days, white Sugar Pea received today instead of desired brown type. Requests dozen brown peas and unplanned extended Gärtner fertility interpretation, including table versus text tensions and possibly biased seed counts. Reading straight through underway; June rereading and October completed abstract later. Berkeley abstract known, not preserved incoming letter. Proposed correspondence with Gärtner does not imply he was alive; apparatus states death 1850. Undated annotations and later October note separately dated. Category labels retained as transcribed.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1665: April 11, supplied 1855. Three blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Curious pea gift received by writing, all kinds new except Queen of Dwarfs; exact arrival not specified. French preservation of giant variety supposed through grouping, not proved practice. Follow-up information conditional; silence would be interpreted as lack of knowledge, not actual negative answer. Gärtner opinion inquiry referred back to 1662; neither outgoing letter becomes incoming prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1699: June 12, supplied 1855. Six blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Missing Berkeley note reports salting experiments; printed approbation distinct source. Wants five-day interval clarified as wet or partly dry; later report omission and Darwin later counting it are apparatus, not current answer. Today accidental drying of eight/ten-week and dried seed series feared lethal, not established germination result. Some seeds actually germinated after 56 days, late germination observed; Hooker interest but little/no persuasion is Darwin assessment. Berkeley peas up; publication and correspondence not merged.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1710: July 3, supplied 1855. Sixteen extracted blocks and footnote; complete raw HTML inspected. Soaking results span species rows and continuing condition phrases: Beet/Rhubarb 65 days cold, Orache 82 cold, Oats/Canary/Capsicum 70 ordinary temperature, Cress/Lettuce/Radish/Carrott 70 with few and delayed germination, Celery/Onion 85. Raw HTML contains only successive paragraphs and no table or retained braces/column structure; this interpretation cannot silently become exact source prose. Layout rendering hold, preserve sequence and ambiguity pending authoritative witness. Peas growing, distinct from initial receipt. No missing incoming prompt required for volunteered progress report.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1386: January 21, supplied 1851. Eight blocks, five footnotes and bibliography. Plates received and pleasing but corrections sent, reversed figures regretted, duplicate Plate II lettering requested and five revises needed. Three specimens and drawings sent with post, no arrival proved. Raw HTML 45 followed by superscript s contains no fraction markup; intended four-fifths is a rendering hold, not forty-five or silently repaired text. Charge asked, later nonpayment not already known. Returning owners specimens future.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1388: February 10, supplied 1851. Nine blocks, five footnotes and bibliography. Most plates approved for printing except I, revised views requested. Main and marginal ridges specifically distinguished, one previously unnoticed error; published lingering ridge in apparatus not substituted for requested deletion. Prior corrections incompletely followed, reason only presumption. Specimen return requested with next revise, not yet received; optional arcuatum supply in postscript.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1389: February 13, supplied 1851. Five blocks, footnote and bibliography. Two specimen boards and scutum enclosed to guide ridge correction; drawings have caused trouble. Both postscripts retained: fees asked, box proposed for Geological Society and notification requested. No delivered box or settled drawing payment established here.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1391: February 19, supplied 1851. Five blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Plate now accepted and specimens all safely arrived by writing, exact arrival not stated. Registered-post cost repaid in stamps; separate drawing charge generously waived/reduced per missing message, but Darwin asks if society estimate included it and still offers payment. This is not final proof of account settlement. Salter reported fossil Balani collection, new loan requested; later seven published specimens not all received now.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-583: Additional prior context read fresh: postmarked November 26, 1840, incomplete one-page ALS. Two surviving blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Fungus hosts compared at uncertain thousand-mile distance, rough field papers return requested. Subsequent 591 corrects host species; do not backpropagate. Berkeley cover list in his hand distinct from Darwin body. No 1855 incoming endpoint.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-591: Additional prior context read fresh: Thursday in supplied March 1841, not exact March 16 paper-reading day. Five blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Berkeley note and enclosure of today received, paper reading anticipated. Corrects 583 by identifying common Fagus betuloides while allowing fungus may also grow on antarctica; not categorical exclusive-host claim. Proof correction requested and later publication apparatus says timely. Hensleigh seen today. Both 583 and 591 outgoing; no synthetic exchange.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1322: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April 28 with supplied 1850 year. Recent missing Sulivan letter from Falklands asks vessel, November expedition and six-week route via Gallegos/St Julian/Bahia Blanca, without salary; fallback £150–200 charter unaffordable. Darwin asks Owen to prompt Beaufort, plans to reply, expects society help unlikely. This current logistical request is not preserved 1845 fossil-discovery letter 730. Thanks prior missing Owen introduction to Mrs Dixon but declines Worthing journey; renews exact plate XXVIII figure 9 Xiphidium request from 1357. Prospectus already sent; hoped lectures publication never completed according to later apparatus. No acquired specimen or successful expedition inferred.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1357: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Friday before April 28, 1850, upper constraint inferred from same plate XXVIII figure 9 request in 1322. Late Mr Dixon and independently supplied 1849 death in 1355 apparatus support a derived 1849–April 27, 1850 window while retaining original open XML lower bound and date uncertainty. Requests this valve and previously discussed figures 3/4; Owen offer to borrow may have been oral or missing correspondence. Conditional favourable answer requested, not actual successful loan. Both this and 1322 are Darwin outgoing; no QA edge between them.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1355: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. September 10 with supplied 1850 year. Requests Dixon cirripede proof sheets; plates have been shown by Sowerby, but prose not yet received/read and volume not published until December. Darwin own fossil volume hopes soon to press, not yet published 1851. Postscript requests specimen and formal permission, gives carrier address split across P3–6 with stray diag/ramme rendering artefacts. 1356 is the accompanying formal note for governing body; it is not an incoming prompt or a reply to 1355. No physical borrowing or disarticulation accomplished here; later B. crenatus identification is not current knowledge.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1356: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Same September 10, 1850 formal request accompanying informal 1355. Asks Owen to lay disarticulation of a small Balanus glacialis specimen before governing body and promises valves returned if permission is granted. No grant or completed destructive examination established. Historical specimen permission is not an instruction to the agent. Same-author enclosure relation, not a back-and-forth conversation.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1354: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. September 10 with supplied 1850 year. Fresh specimens reveal probable conflation of two species under undulatum; now requests six added views and discusses plate space/deletions. Raw HTML has literal [Diagram] and [/Diagram] enclosing a numbered textual specification, zero image or table nodes; separate diagrams sent are not preserved merely because placeholder exists. Maintain views, sizes and proximity constraints without synthetic image reconstruction. Supplies better validus specimen, requests tracing of altered woodcut, permits extra paid work through Bowerbank. Possible deletions are options, not final omissions: later all Hausmanni figures retained. Proof comparison and London trip remain planned.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1358: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. September 12 with supplied 1850 year. Approves revised woodcut but corrects upper lateral to Upper Latus with capital L and cardinal to Carinal. Raw text includes capital L instruction; do not merge it into scientific term. Requests four blocks close to type, explains proposed cutter arrangement and actual extra porterage payment. Wants proofs only when all four plates ready, plus woodcut proofs, blocks retained by Sowerby. Later five-plate final volume differs from current four-plate expectation; not an arithmetic error to repair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1360: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. September 23 with supplied 1850 year. New German specimen is unfamiliar and near validus; enclosed view initially expected as woodcut because no plate space. P5 revises P1 instruction: instead of sending block first, inspect during intended London proof visit. Requests two proofs of each plate and advance notice, not actual possession. Later artist fits view in plate; preserve original intention rather than final outcome. Dunker/Roemer identification in apparatus is source attribution not preserved incoming cover. Enclosed drawing absent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1368: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. November 11 with supplied 1850 year. Replies late to missing Sowerby letter after illness, evaluates received rough proof, requests corrections, divisions and labels, needs rough sheet preserved with final proof. Does not claim all plates received or finished. Fitch missing letter threatens return; several previous apologies, no full prompt text. Changes transport plan to servant and tax-cart for proofs/specimens, reserving Loricula plate for later, asks whether Wetherell specimen returned and gracilis registered parcel received six weeks earlier. Questions are not proof return/delivery happened. Same-date 1369 tells Fitch one of five plates received; both are Darwin outgoing witnesses, not a QA pair.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1667: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April 13 with supplied 1855 year, written BY Darwin. Requests a list of twelve superior Royal Society candidates; he is not supplying that list here. Asks to borrow an old Lawsonian synopsis because purchase failed and explains intended erasable marks. Berkeley peas received; forty-five varieties are planned together. He doubts the lady water-bug ova story without better information. P4 replies to a missing Hooker seed note, declines the suggested scale, reports one-week success and varied germination rather than universal survival, and plants the fourteen-day batch today. Temperature and flow calculations are historical claims. P5 sends his Gray naturalised-plant list for advice and describes masking names before selection to avoid bias; enclosed list is not transcribed here. P7 records unsalted comparison and glass tumblers. Old March library/winglessness letters are not the missing seed response.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-13872: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. December 31 in mutually exclusive 1852 OR 1853; unknown recipient. Four blocks, seven footnotes and bibliography. Coquimbo shell discussion cites own book and distinguishes Sowerby, d Orbigny and own species judgments. Bed age Miocene or Eocene explicitly uncertain; genus and species criteria differ. Period assignment inferred from no reference to 1854 cirripede volume, not independently exact year. Modern synonyms and later classifications remain apparatus. Missing request not inferred from generic scientific topic.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
